Emily — attaching the high-level eval and model notes (attached: acme_eval_report_v1.pdf). Key highlights below: 

- Recommended models for initial POC (tradeoff summary):
  * redwood-770m-quant (low-latency, cost-efficient, good for short, high-throughput summaries)
  * redwood-1.3b (better coherence on longer summaries, modest latency increase)
  * Llama2-13B-8k-quant (strong quality baseline for complex narratives; higher cost; use as fallback for heavy cases)

- Benchmarks (summary):
  * redwood-770m-quant: median token-latency 45ms/token (single stream), median end-to-end short-summary p95 ~ 420ms, token cost estimate: ~$0.002 per summary (depends on prompt length).
  * redwood-1.3b: median token-latency 70ms/token, p95 ~ 580ms.
  * Llama2-13B-8k-quant: p95 ~ 1.1s for short summaries.

- Quality/regression notes: we ran your prompt set across 200 clinical examples. We flagged 6 regression cases where the model truncated the last sentence when streaming is enabled (root cause: early stop tokens emitted due to prompt suffix ambiguity in our decoding config). Full details in acme_eval_report_v1.pdf (see section "Streaming truncation cases").

- Immediate mitigations that helped in our test runs:
  * Use explicit stop sequences tied to clinical separators (e.g., "
### END SUMMARY###
").
  * Move critical trailing instructions into a separate completion step (post-stream finalize pass) for safety-critical closing lines.
  * Tune decoding: prefer top-p sampling with tempered nucleus (top_p 0.9) and avoid aggressive early-stopping logits thresholds.

Action items I can take now:
- Book the POC for 3/25-3/26 morning PT (Jordan to lead the tech session).
- Run one short smoke test on 20 of your clinical prompts using redwood-770m-quant with streaming-on and attach logs for the truncation cases.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Emily / Liam — quick tech note ahead of the POC. Below are the troubleshooting steps and recommended streaming config we'll test. Please forward any logs you already have from your side.

Reproducing partial-output / truncation behavior:
1) Confirm client-side assembly: ensure the UI concatenates stream chunks in order and only applies final stop-sequence processing after the last chunk.
2) Server-side: check decoding config for premature eos_threshold or short-circuiting. If set, set eos_threshold to a conservative value or disable for streaming.

Recommended streaming config for POC (low-risk defaults):
- model: redwood-770m-quant (start)
- max_new_tokens: 250
- stream_chunk_size: 32 tokens (reduces wall-clock serialization delay while keeping chunk coherency)
- stop_sequences: ["### END SUMMARY###", "

"] (explicit clinical separators)
- decoding: top_p 0.92, temperature 0.7, disable early-eos heuristics
- batching: client-side batching 1 for lower latency; server continuous batching enabled to merge similar seq-length requests at the runtime layer

Latency and SLOs: with the above we expect median end-to-end p50 < 350ms for short summaries and p95 < 650ms in our dedicated environment; production cloud SLO will vary with network and client assembly logic.

Logging/diagnostics we'll collect during the POC:
- token-level timestamps (server/edge)
- final output checksums vs. non-streamed run
- early-eos events and token logits snapshots for flagged cases

I'll lead the live debugging on the call. If you can share a few sample transcripts where you saw truncation ahead of time, I can pre-seed the test harness.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
